niche: a municipal retrofit lottery's measured savings carried by building type and works age to the next grant round's applicants, and the round's settled cost once late applications and withdrawals are in
answer: Fund insulation and heating controls in the 2026 round, not heating optimisation: on the applications received €88.24, €98.60 and €157.82 of grant per lifetime tonne against €120 (90% ranges €83.12 to €93.38, €90.27 to €109.84, €122.26 to €229.48); the funded round's applications ask for €7,738,505 and it pays €7,262,823; the pilot's works saved 3,303 tonnes of CO2 in 2025/26
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst cleans the meter reads, normalises each season as the utility does and reads the lottery as drawn, which gets each measure's saving by season right, then takes each measure's pooled seven-season saving, carries it flat over the measure's life, prices this year's applications at that one rate per measure and scales the received grant by the 2019 share in by 12 June: it funds insulation and heating optimisation and not controls, and books the round below what it will pay, because heating optimisation's saving fades with the works' age, the pilot's controls rate is diluted by round-the-clock buildings few of this year's applicants are, and the late insulation applications run larger and withdraw more.
domain_test: The results are measurement and verification quantities on weather-normalised gas use: a lottery's metered savings by works age, their persistence over a measure's service life, their dependence on how a building is occupied and how much of its gas goes to hot water, carried into grant per lifetime tonne of CO2; with another field's nouns there is no degree-day normalisation, no hot-water share that caps what insulation can save, no setback that saves nothing in a building heated round the clock, and no heating curve that creeps back up after an optimisation.

driver: The decisive quantities are a randomised effect carried to a forward population and horizon the trial never observed: each option's effect differs by the kind of unit and fades with the treatment's age at rates that differ by option, so the trial's pooled average misstates what the forward round's own units would gain over each option's life, and the round's settled cost needs the late arrivals, which run larger and drop out more, projected by option; different shortcuts fund different options.
driver_concrete: Haldenau's 2019 retrofit lottery gives each measure's normal-weather gas saving against the passed-over owners season by season; heating optimisation's saving fades with the works' age, heating controls save almost nothing in the care homes and hotels that made up much of the pilot's controls buildings but few of this year's applicants, and late insulation applications run larger and withdraw more, so the 2026 round funds insulation and controls, not heating optimisation, and the round's settled grant is projected measure by measure.
stump: A careful but hurried solver takes each measure's pooled seven-season lottery saving, carries it flat over the measure's life, prices this year's applications at that rate and scales the received grant by the 2019 share in by 12 June: it funds insulation and heating optimisation and not controls and books the round short, because heating optimisation's saving fades, the pilot's controls rate is diluted by round-the-clock buildings, and the late applications run larger and withdraw more.

differentiation.mark132: mark132 ages a wear-out failure rate and corrects it for renewal by a new item; here a treatment effect fades with the works' age and is integrated over a service life with no renewal, and that is one result of eight beside a transport by type, the round projected at close and the pilot's season saving.
differentiation.mark175: mark175 reads each unit's take-up at its own run's fill and carries it to new places; here a randomised saving is carried by how a building is occupied to this year's applicants and by works age over each measure's life, and the round's grant is projected from the pilot's response timing, sizes and withdrawals.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many of the period's placeable units a fixed team can finish before the period closes, because each unit counts only once that team performs one last step for it, the team's spare weekly capacity is visible only as the ceiling it held through an earlier unrelated surge, and the decision's own volume, bunched by its filed calendar into weeks no closed period approached, queues the later units past the close; the closed record's lag and an annual capacity check both pass, so the placeable count overstates the in-period total wherever the team is small and the units are many.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what a unit's security fetches if the unit fails, which the record measures by an inspection made at the failure while the forward units carry only a market index rolled forward from an earlier inspection; the security of units that fail falls behind the index by more the longer since that inspection, and the forward units were inspected longer ago than the record's failures mostly were, so the rolled-forward index overstates what the failing units will fetch.

The decisive quantity is the effect of a treatment assigned by lottery, where the units the lottery passed over were reached one area at a time by a second programme that skipped the winners and moved the same outcome for good, so the randomised comparison narrows period by period as if the effect faded; only passed-over units the second programme had not yet reached give the counterfactual, and the effect then decides which options a forward round funds against a cost-per-unit limit.
lineage.driver_concrete: Haldenau's 2019 retrofit pilot drew its places by lot among the owners who answered the benchmarking notice's offer, so the owners passed over are the natural comparison; but the utility's service team tuned the burners of most of them, district by district from September 2019, and skipped every building with pilot works, so the passed-over buildings' gas use steps down and the measures' savings appear to fade; set against passed-over buildings not yet tuned, the savings hold, and heating optimisation clears the council's cost-per-tonne limit.
lineage.stump: A competent solver reads the pilot as the randomised trial it was drawn as, measures each measure's saving as the works buildings' weather-normalised gas use against the passed-over buildings' on the notice season, sees the gap narrow every season and averages it or reads it as savings fading, and funds insulation alone in 2026; the step that lands it there is trusting a comparison whose buildings the service team was tuning district by district while it skipped the works buildings, when against passed-over buildings not yet tuned heating optimisation saves about six per cent and clears the limit.
